newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday June 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday June 11.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) leader Massimo D'Alema, the head of a bicameral commission aimed at carrying out constitutional reforms, said that without an agreement about the electoral system the whole commission could easily collapse (all).
* Prime minister Romano Prodi said Italy had never asked to bring forward the launch of European economic and monetary union (all).

* In an interview, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco called France's request for some extra time to reflect on the EMU stability pact and its emphasis on the need to create new jobs as fair and comprehensible. Visco also stressed the important role of politics in European economic and monetary union (Corriere della Sera).

* The Ministry of Transport said Italian new car registrations rose 43.23 percent to 232,600 units in May compared with 162,399 in May 1996. New car registrations in May for the Fiat group rose 45.2 percent to 101,600 from May 1996, but fell 2.2 percent from April 1997 (all).

* A consortium led by Spain's utility Endesa and Italy's STET looks set to win 60 percent of Spain's second telephone operator Retevision at auction after dranatically outbidding its competitor. The Endesa/STET group said its offer for the initial privatisation of Retevision was 116.36 billion pesetas (Corriere della Sera).

* Alberto Zuliani, head of national statistics office ISTAT, said the latest data suggests the Italian economy is picking up, meaning that the government might still meet its target of 1.2 percent economic growth this year. Zuliani also said Italian industrial production is expected to rise an unadjusted 1.2 percent in the second quarter of 1997 in comparison with the first quarter, when output fell 0.9 percent (all).

* A report by national statistics institute ISTAT showed Italy had a 3.604 trillion lire trade surplus with non-European Union countries in April. ISTAT also said Italy had a global trade surplus in March of 4.428 trillion lire against a surplus of 5.307 trillion lire in March 1996 (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
